subject: Hosted evaluation: Quickstart checklist, prefetch slice & rate plan
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Goldberg <ari.goldberg@finlytics.ai>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted evaluation: Quickstart checklist, prefetch slice & rate plan

Ari / Sanjay — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can scope a Hosted evaluation that lines up with FinLytics' latency and cost targets. TL;DR: Hosted makes sense as a first-phase for product validation; Dedicated or Private can follow if isolation/SLA needs increase.

What we covered today:
- Primary use: document summarization + customer support triage (low-latency snippets, 1–3s target median).
- Expected steady-state: ~45 QPS during business hours, spike to ~180 QPS for batch jobs (30–60s bursts).
- Preferred approach: start on Hosted API sandbox -> production sandbox slice -> canary -> ramp.

Proposed next steps for the evaluation (please confirm):
1) Traffic profile: confirm avg QPS, burst behavior, token distribution (attached traffic-slice-proposal.csv).
2) Quickstart access: we can provision a hosted sandbox with two endpoints: "summarize-v1" (short outputs) and "triage-v1" (longer context + retrieval).
3) Rate limits & routing: default rate tiers we recommend are 60r/s, 180r/s, and 300r/s (per-tenant). We can gate the sandbox at 120r/s to match expected spikes.
4) Prefetch / prefix caching: for summarize-v1 we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for frequent prompts — reduces token cost by ~15–30% on repeated contexts.
5) Security/compliance: Hosted will be under our standard processing; if you require VPC or on-prem for audit reasons we can scope Private in parallel.

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf (ops steps), traffic-slice-proposal.csv (sample QPS timeline).

Can you reply with: (A) confirmation of steady-state and peak QPS numbers, (B) any internal must-haves (VPC/KMS/SOC2 evidence), and (C) who should be on the technical kickoff? I can book a 30-min sandbox provisioning slot once we have those.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Ari Goldberg <ari.goldberg@finlytics.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-17T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: Quickstart checklist, prefetch slice & rate plan

Thanks, Nikhil — useful recap. Quick answers below and one question.

A) Traffic profile: steady-state ~40–50 QPS (US hours), known nightly batch that can hit ~160–180 QPS for 5–10 minutes. Token distribution: average prompt 180 tokens in, 120 tokens out (triage), summarize is ~40 tokens out.
B) Must-haves: SOC2 evidence is critical; KMS integration preferred but not blocker for the pilot. We do not need on-prem for the pilot.
C) Tech kickoff: looping in Sanjay (eng) and me.

Question: can you confirm how the hosted sandbox enforces per-endpoint rate caps? We have two teams that will hit different endpoints and want isolation so one team's spike doesn't throttle the other.

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Goldberg <ari.goldberg@finlytics.ai>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: Quickstart checklist, prefetch slice & rate plan

Ari — thanks for the quick turnaround. Short answers and a configuration suggestion below.

Per-endpoint isolation: Hosted enforces rate caps at the endpoint level by default. We can map each logical team to a dedicated endpoint + token so you get independent rate ceilings and accounting. Examples we will provision for the sandbox:
- finlytics-summarize (rate cap 120r/s)
- finlytics-triage (rate cap 120r/s, burst up to 180r/s for short windows)

If you prefer hard isolation between teams we can create separate API keys and endpoint partitions; that way a heavy triage job won't consume summarize capacity. We'll surface token-level cost and latency per endpoint in the console.

Prefetch / KV caching: for summarize-v1 enable prefix caching for the top ~200 prompt templates you expect to reuse. In practice this reduces token spend and improves p95 latency for repeated contexts. We'll include a short instruction set in the quickstart PDF (see redwood-quickstart-checklist.pdf).

Provisioning plan:
- Stage 1 (sandbox): provision two endpoints, rate caps as above, SOC2 evidence pack, KMS test key option.
- Stage 2 (production sandbox canary): narrow-slice of traffic (5% prod traffic) with observability hooks.
- Stage 3 (ramp): move to higher rate tier or discuss Dedicated capacity if consistent 24/7 throughput > 200r/s

I attached a sample mapping in traffic-slice-proposal.csv. If that looks good I'll schedule the 30-min provisioning window tomorrow at 10am PT.

Links: Quickstart docs: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/quickstart-hosted
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/DL-4721
